why: Habakkuk 1:6 names the Chaldeans, the Babylonian people God raises up; Bible Atlas does not link this verse.
Habakkuk 3:7 means the land and people of Midian, not Midian the son of Abraham.

Bible Atlas puts Cushan on the same point as Cush in Nubia, but Habakkuk 3:7 sets Cushan in parallel with Midian, so it was probably in northwest Arabia. Its location is uncertain, so no dot is drawn here.
